caveat: These numbers come from retraining this type of detector with one kind of music left out and testing it on what it had not seen. 'Accuracy' here is the average of two shares, AI tracks caught and human tracks correctly passed, so 50% is a coin flip. On songs by new artists whose music resembles its training data, its accuracy was 89% and it wrongly called 8% of human songs AI-generated. On music from a site it never trained on, it did worse: retrained without FMA (the Free Music Archive), it wrongly called 14% of FMA's pre-2010 tracks AI-generated; retrained without Jamendo (another free-music site), 28% of Jamendo tracks. Those counts treat a P(AI) of 0.5 or above as an AI call; this tool says 'likely AI-generated' only at 0.8 or above, which still flagged 4% of those FMA tracks and 14% of those Jamendo tracks, and called 30% and 35% 'uncertain'. Treat these as estimates of how often it accuses real musicians whose music is unlike its training data (the copy used here did train on FMA, Jamendo and some GuitarSet solo-guitar recordings). Retrained without one AI music generator, it caught 69% of that generator's tracks on average (worst: Riffusion v1, 9%); with a whole family of models left out (like music from a new company), as few as 42% (all Udio versions). Retrained on songs with vocals only, its accuracy on instrumentals was 69%, partly because 60% of the AI instrumentals in that test came from generators missing from its vocal training, and it wrongly called 23% of human instrumentals AI-generated (10% when trained on instrumentals). Retrained on instrumentals only, its accuracy on songs with vocals was 85%; there, too, 25% of the AI songs came from generators missing from its training. Rates are per 10-second excerpt. Everyday edits that hurt it most: pitch raised 2 semitones (accuracy 82%), pitch lowered 2 semitones (84%) and made 10% faster with pitch kept (85%), against 89% unedited. Old or lo-fi human recordings are still wrongly called AI more often: 24% of the 123 pre-2010 FMA tracks with almost no sound above 8 kHz, against 12% of the other 676. A score is one piece of evidence, never proof that a musician used AI.
